sources.entry: Caddy - Powerful, enterprise-ready, open source web server with automatic HTTPS. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Go/deb/Docker
Caddy | Fast, multi-platform web server with automatic HTTPS

summary.one_liner: Caddy is an extensible Go web server and reverse proxy platform that enables HTTPS automatically and by default.
summary.what_it_does: Caddy serves HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3 by default and obtains and renews TLS certificates automatically from ZeroSSL or Let's Encrypt for public names. For internal names and IPs it uses a built-in managed local CA. Configuration can be written in the Caddyfile, native JSON, or other formats converted through config adapters (JSON 5, YAML, TOML, NGINX config, and more), and can be changed at runtime through a JSON API. Caddy is built as a platform of modules ("apps"), with the `tls` and `http` apps shipped as standard. The README says it has no external dependencies and can run anywhere. Developers can build it from source or with the xcaddy tool to add plugins and version information.
use_cases: serve a website over HTTPS with automatic certificates
run a local certificate authority for internal names
configure a web server through a JSON API
build a custom Go server with plugins
how_to_run: Download Caddy from GitHub Releases and place the executable in your PATH
git clone the repository, cd into caddy/cmd/caddy/, and run go build (development build without version info)
Install the xcaddy builder and run xcaddy build to add plugins or version information
Run go test ./... to execute the test suite
notable: Automatic HTTPS by default, with multi-issuer fallback and encrypted ClientHello (ECH) support
Configurable with the Caddyfile, native JSON, a runtime JSON API, or config adapters
Modular plugin architecture where Caddy apps are Go modules
Supports HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3 by default
caveats: Binding to low ports on Linux requires setting capabilities (setcap) for a development build
Source builds require Go 1.26.0 or newer
The README says the name "Caddy" is trademarked and asks users not to call it "Caddy Server" or "CaddyServer"
